 Hon'Ble Samit Gopal, J.

2. Heard Sri Rakesh Dubey, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Birendra Pratap Singh, learned counsel for the State and perused the record.

3. This bail application under Section 483 of B.N.S.S. has been filed by the applicant Rajveer,
seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No. 26 of 2023, under Section(s) 498A, 304B I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, registered at P.S.- Amrahat, District- Kanpur Dehat.

4. The first information report of the present matter was lodged on 16.8.2023 by Smt. Meera Devi against the applicant, Chhunni Devi and Bhajanlal@Guddu alleging therein that the marriage of her daughter Suvi@Anjali was solemnized with Rajveer (the applicant) around a year back and things were going right.
But later on the accused persons started torturing and assaulting her which was told by her daughter on phone.

On 16.8.2023 at about 3.30 p.m. she received information on her phone that her daughter has consumed some poisonous substance, after which she went to her house and found her body lying in the courtyard.
The accused persons have forcefully gave her some poison and murdered her.
A report be lodged and action be taken.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that although the applicant is husband of the deceased but he has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is submitted while placing para-24 of the affidavit that the prosecution story shows that it is not a case of forceful administration of poison.

Further while placing para-25 of the affidavit it is submitted that the present case is not a case of dowry death and the prosecution has failed to establish that the applicant at any point of time demanded dowry from the informant and his family members and inflicted cruelty with the deceased due to it.

It is further submitted while placing para-26 of the affidavit that the deceased was feeling defamed as the marriage was inter-caste marriage and some distant relatives had taunted her due to which she committed suicide and took the extreme step.
It is submitted that there is no specification of demand of dowry in the F.I.R. and as such the same is vague.

Further while placing the statements of the independent witnesses namely Smt. Jyoti, Dhaniram and Veer Singh it is submitted that they have stated that the deceased consumed some poisonous substance and suffered vomiting and at that point of time the accused persons were not present at the house.
It is submitted that the applicant is having no criminal history as stated in para-34 of the affidavit and is in jail since 5.6.2024.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the State vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that the applicant is the husband of the deceased.
The viscera of the deceased was found to contain Organochloro Insecticides in it.

It is submitted that the deceased died an unnatural death within Rajveer vs State Of U.P. on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45163718/
2 seven years of marriage in her matrimonial house and there is an allegation of demand of dowry against the applicant and other co-accused persons.
7. After having heard learned counsel for the parties and perusing the record, it is evident that the applicant is the husband of the deceased.
There is an allegation of demand of dowry, torture and harassment by the applicant and other co-accused persons.
The deceased died unnaturally within seven years of marriage in her matrimonial house.
The reasons as are being disclosed in paragraph- 24, 25 and 26 of the affidavit do not inspire confidence.

8. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court does not find it a fit case for bail,
hence, the bail application is rejected.
9. Pending application (s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
(Samit Gopal,J.) November 4, 2025 Naresh  Rajveer vs State Of U.P. on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45163718/
